name: Accessibility
summary: Make your apps accessible to everyone who uses Apple devices.

declarations.name: AccessibilityNotification
declarations.comment: An accessibility notification that an app can send.

declarations.name: AccessibilityNotification.Announcement
declarations.comment:
A notification that an app posts when it needs to convey an
announcement to the assistive app. Include an announcement value,
such as `String` or `AttributedString`, that an assistive app will
announce.

declarations.name: AccessibilityNotification.LayoutChanged
declarations.comment:
A notification that an app posts when the layout of a screen changes.
Optionally, include a parameter that contains the accessibility element
for VoiceOver to move to after processing the notification.

declarations.name: AccessibilityNotification.PageScrolled
declarations.comment:
A notification that an app posts when a scroll action completes.
Include an announcement value, such as `String` or `AttributedString`,
that an assistive app will announce. When an assistive app repeatedly
receives the same scroll position value, it indicates to users that
scrolling can't continue due to a border or boundary.

declarations.name: AccessibilityNotification.ScreenChanged
declarations.comment:
A notification that an app posts when a new view appears that occupies
a major portion of the screen. Optionally, include a parameter that
contains the accessibility element for VoiceOver to move to after
processing the notification.

declarations.name: AttributeScopes.AccessibilityAttributes.AdjustedPitchAttribute
declarations.comment:
An attribute to adjust the pitch the spoken speech.

Values between `-1` and `0` result in a lower pitch while
values between `0` and `1` result in a higher pitch.

For example, you may want to lower the pitch when
an object is deleted, or raise the pitch if an object is inserted.

declarations.name: AttributeScopes.AccessibilityAttributes.AnnouncementPriorityAttribute
declarations.comment:
An attribute to define the urgency of the announcement.

For example, when `low` is specified, announcements are queued
and spoken when other speech utterances have completed. When
`default` is specified, announcements will interrupt existing speech,
but are interruptible if a new speech utterance is started. When `high`
is specified, announcements will interrupt other speech and cannot be
interrupted once started.

declarations.name: AttributeScopes.AccessibilityAttributes.HeadingLevelAttribute
declarations.comment:
An attribute for the level of this heading.

Assistive technologies can use this property to improve
navigation and describe the level number of levels
``HeadingLevel/h1`` through ``HeadingLevel/h6``
alongside the text.

For example, you can rank sections within UI using a heading level.
The most important section is marked with``HeadingLevel/h1``.
Nested sections can use subsequent heading levels. For unranked
headings, use ``HeadingLevel/unspecified``.

declarations.name: AttributeScopes.AccessibilityAttributes.IPANotationAttribute
declarations.comment:
An attribute to define the International Phonetic Alphabet
representation for speech.

The IPA representation defines pronunciation of words that
have the same spelling but different sounds.

For example, consider the different pronunciations of the word
"live" in the following two sentences:

 - "Anne wants to live on Main Street."
 - "Maria wants to go to the live concert."

In the first sentence, “live” rhymes with "give."  Its IPA representation
would be “lɪv”. In the second sentence, it rhymes with "hive". Its
IPA representation would be “laɪv”.

- Note: This attribute is not used on macOS

declarations.name: AttributeScopes.AccessibilityAttributes.QueueAnnouncementAttribute
declarations.comment:
An attribute to define if speech announcements spoken
by VoiceOver should be queued behind existing speech
rather than interrupting speech in progress.

When `true`, the announcement will be queued behind
existing speech. When `false`, it will interrupt existing speech.
By default, announcements interrupt existing speech.

- Note: This attribute is not used on macOS

declarations.name: AttributeScopes.AccessibilityAttributes.SpeechSSMLAttribute
declarations.comment:
An attribute for an SSML fragment describing how the annotated range should be spoken.

The value is an SSML fragment string. Assistive technologies that produce speech
use the fragment to determine pronunciation, language, pacing, and emphasis for
the annotated range. Non-speech clients (e.g. Braille) ignore this attribute.

When present, this attribute takes precedence over the older single-purpose
speech attributes (IPA notation, spell out, pitch, punctuation, language).

declarations.comment:
An attribute to define if each character should be spoken separately.

For example, a number representing a series of digits, like 25,
spoken as "two-five" rather than "twenty-five". Another usecase
is acronyms, like APPL, spoken as "A-P-P-L"

declarations.name: AttributeScopes.AccessibilityAttributes.TextualContextAttribute
declarations.comment:
An attribute for the textual context.

Assistive technologies can use this property to choose
an appropriate way to output the text. For example, when
encountering a source coding context, VoiceOver could
choose to speak all punctuation.

- Note: This attribute is not used on macOS
